EU Services Employment Structure

Source: Eurostat LFS · persons aged 15-64 (20-64 for occupation data)
Employment structure Job quality Pay & output Who works there

Ten headline findings from the data on this site. Each links through to the relevant section with the right filters already applied.

1
Services grew from 99.0 million to 116.3 million workers since 2008 (+17.7%), while its share of total EU27 employment rose from 52.3% to 58.0% — growth in both absolute and relative terms.
Sector Overview →
2
Within services, Trade is the largest sub-sector (23.2%, but declining from 27.3% in 2008). Health & social work is second (19.6%, growing). Professional & scientific services is third (10.4%) and growing.
Within Services →
3
Info & Communication rose from 5.1% to 6.8% of services employment since 2008 — a roughly one-third increase in its share, the fastest-rising sub-sector on the site.
Sub-sector Deep Dive →
4
ICT's growth is almost entirely a "Professionals" story: employment in that occupation within Info & Communication rose from 1.85 million to 4.8 million since 2008 (+2.95 million) — the largest single occupation-sector shift measured anywhere in the data.
Occupation × Sector →
5
Services' part-time rate (23.5%) is roughly triple Industry's (7.4%) — and notably, it's now even higher than Public services' (19.3%).
Part-time & Temporary →
6
Services has the highest "recently-started job" rate of any broad sector (4.4%, a job-churn proxy) — and within services, that churn is heavily concentrated in Accommodation & Food (8.3%) and Household employers (6.9%).
Recent Hires & Turnover →
7
Services has the shortest average working week of the four broad sectors (35.6 hrs). This is partly explained by services' much higher part-time rate (23.5% vs. 7.4% in Industry).
Working Hours →
8
Finance (€67,820) and ICT (€62,910) are the two best-paying service sub-sectors, both comfortably outpacing Public admin/education/health combined (€48,230). Arts & other services is the lowest-paid service sub-sector (€32,910/year) — barely above Construction and less than half of Finance's pay level.
Compensation →
9
Financial & insurance combines high pay (€67,820) with low churn (2.5% recent hires) — the most "stable, well-paid" profile in services; Accommodation & Food sits at the opposite end on both counts.
Compensation →
10
Fatal accidents are far more frequent in Agriculture (5.98 per 100,000) and Industry (5.12) than in services overall. Within services, they are heavily concentrated in Transport & storage (4.92) — nearly 3x the next-highest services sub-sector.
Health & Safety →
11
Transport & storage is the most dangerous services sub-sector by both measures, but the pattern shifts for less severe injuries: Admin & support has the second-highest non-fatal accident rate (2,043 per 100,000) despite one of the lowest fatal rates — suggesting frequent but rarely deadly incidents, unlike Agriculture and Industry where accidents are less common but far more often fatal.
Health & Safety →
